items.title: Commencement
notes:
A meeting of City Council was held at 11:33 a.m. this date, chaired by Mayor B. Vrbanovic. Notice of this meeting had been previously given to all members of Council by the City Clerk pursuant to Chapter 25 (Council Procedure) of the Municipal Code.

The meeting began with a Land Acknowledgement given by the Mayor.

items.title: Shaping the 2027–2030 Strategic Plan: Process Overview and Identification of Key Themes for Further Exploration, CAO-2026-202
notes:
Council considered Chief Administrative Officer's report CAO-2026-202, entitled Shaping the 2027–2030 Strategic Plan: Process Overview and Identification of Key Themes for Further Exploration, dated April 29, 2026, related to the the 2027-2030 strategic planning process, timeline, key inputs, and early insights from a community survey and United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Voluntary Local Review (VLR).

M. Love provided opening remarks. K. Rieger then introduced D. Coletto, Abacus Data who provided a presentation on the research findings of a resident satisfaction survey conducted in the City of Kitchener to inform the 2027-2030 strategic plan. D. Coletto noted that, overall, the results of the survey were significantly higher than findings of comparable municipalities and a national dataset. D. Coletto explained that the results of the community survey indicate that affordability and growth have become the dominant factors shaping how residents evaluate the City, resulting in a widening gap between residents’ current satisfaction with City services and their confidence in the City’s ability to maintain those services as the population grows. 

J. Young provided remarks on behalf of Compass Kitchener noting, the survey results align with the Committee’s expectation for affordability and cost of living to be the top issues facing the community. J. Young further noted that, the Committee is interested in learning more about how the survey responses varied across different age groups.

K. Rieger then introduced J. Beale, Program Director, Local Futures, University of Waterloo who provided a presentation on the early insights of a Voluntary Local Review of the City's alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). J. Beale reported that the City of Kitchener’s alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) was determined to be 66.9%, indicating a strong correlation between the City’s strategies and plans and the targets set out in the global SDG framework. J. Beale further explained that the City's performance gaps are primarily concentrated in the equity, inclusion, and governance-related SDGs due to an absence of formal policy frameworks that link initiatives to measurable outcomes.  

K. Rieger requested Council’s feedback on the presentations and sought direction on which areas or themes staff should further examine. 

Councillor A. Owodunni left the meeting at this time and re-entered.
